Yes, the story has an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition. 

The majority of the story unfolds in real-time through vivid, engaging scenes—driving in the Volvo, walking along Popham Beach, drinking wine in the dunes, and sitting in the stalled car in the rain. These scenes rely heavily on sharp dialogue and sensory details to build emotional tension between Arthur and Clara. However, the author seamlessly weaves concise passages of summary and exposition into the early scenes to compress the preceding twenty-seven days at the artists' colony and provide necessary background about their lives back in Chicago and Brooklyn. This balance allows the reader to understand the history and stakes of their fleeting romance without interrupting the immediate momentum and intimacy of their final afternoon together.
